upper_bound.quote: This is a common-refinement (overlay) construction: superimpose the concatenated intervals of $B$ on an initial segment of length $q$ of the concatenated intervals of $A$, cut both rows at the union of the division points and pair the corresponding cells; the bound on the number of cuts follows by counting the cells of the common refinement (standard; details omitted).
upper_bound.witness: The missing statement is a proof, for arbitrary disjoint nonempty collections A and B, that the described overlay can be implemented by at most |A|+|B|-1 new marks while pairing all of B with equal-length material from A and leaving exactly p-q unpaired. The passage explicitly omits the required cut-count details.
upper_bound.load_bearing: The upper bound uses this lemma to obtain the total cut estimate (13). Without the omitted uniform cut-count proof, Xiang Yu's proposed response has not been shown to respect the limit of n marks.

parsed.notes: The stated closed form is correct. The reduction and powers-of-two lower bound are fully argued, but the upper bound depends on a common-refinement lemma whose decisive cut-count proof is expressly omitted.
